# Mission 1

## Hallway Analysis

Well around people any sudden movements or turns would be concerning for someone nearby. If in a crowded area I would keep the turns to a minimum if possible, but at the same time any abrupt stops could also be frustrating for those around it. To address these we might want to decrease the angular velocity so that its turns are less fast and more predictable. 

## Trial Synthesis

In all three trials the shape of the path all lined up with my predictions. The heading changes from the actual odometry always were close but fell short of the predicted distance/turns. For example, in trial 2 by 0.170 rad and in trial 3 by 0.164. Trial 2 had the largest difference, the heading was off by -0.170 rad which a little under 10 degrees. A likely cause of this could be that the odometry calibration is a little off or there is some wheel slip action happening. To test this we could run multiple runs of just turning trials and then multiple of just driving forward trials, we will then measure that distance and if there is a consistent percent error then there is a problem with calibration and we can adjust that, but if the error is worse then it will most likely be a slip issue. My prediction for d = 0.9m.
